operation_details.item: The user always chooses only free public data sources for market research and avoids paid databases.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For the competitive benchmarking analysis, we can compare revenue growth, operating margins, customer acquisition costs, and market share across selected healthcare companies. Do you have a preferred approach to sourcing the market data?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For market research subscriptions, I always choose only free public data sources and avoid paid databases even when accuracy and timeliness matter.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. We can build the analysis around public filings, government datasets, regulatory publications, investor presentations, company websites, and publicly available industry reports.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That works. I want the process to be repeatable so the budget team can refresh the analysis without adding a recurring data subscription.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A practical workflow would be to document each source, publication date, reporting period, extraction method, and any assumptions. We can also assign confidence ratings to metrics that are less directly comparable.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Please prioritize sources that provide downloadable historical data. I would rather spend time reconciling definitions than introduce a paid database into the budget.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For healthcare benchmarking, I suggest starting with SEC filings and company annual reports for financial measures, CMS and other government datasets for utilization or spending measures, and public earnings materials for management commentary.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Include a source matrix with the metric, company coverage, reporting frequency, historical depth, URL, and the date each figure was retrieved.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I will structure the matrix that way and flag gaps where companies use different segment definitions or fiscal calendars. The final workbook can include a documented normalization layer before calculating peer averages.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Good. Begin with a shortlist of free public sources for five comparable healthcare companies, then outline the calculations for margins, growth rates, and any available market-share indicators.
